title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 13
statement: Exhibit a set \(S\) which tiles the integers \(\mathbf{Z}\) but not the natural numbers \(\mathbf{N}\).

solutions.text: One example is \(\{1,3,4,6\}\). Since its elements are all distinct modulo 4 , it tiles \(\mathbf{Z}\) by translation by multiples of 4 . On the other hand, it is easy to see that it cannot tile \(\mathbf{N}\) : 1 is contained in \(\{1,3,4,6\}\), but then there is no possible set for 2 to be contained in that does not overlap. Another example is \(\{1,2,6\}\).
